item.title: Celadon industry upgraded in Longquan, China's Zhejiang
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
A staff member livestreams at a studio of the Longquan celadon in Longquan, east China's Zhejiang Province, Oct. 14, 2026. Located in southwestern Zhejiang Province, Longquan City boasts abundant ceramic clay, dense forests, and the Longquan River, providing ideal conditions for its celadon industry. Longquan celadon firing technique was listed as a national intangible cultural heritage in 2006 and was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2009. In recent years, Longquan has upgraded its celadon industry by improving the quality of raw material, boosting industrial intelligence and empowering innovation. Today, the city has over 3,000 celadon-related businesses with more than 23,000 workers involved. item.title: International visitors explore four decades of greening in Xinjiang's Kekeya
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
AKSU, Xinjiang, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- After viewing photographs of the area's earlier landscape at the Kekeya Memorial Hall in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, American actor and television presenter Steven Weathers was impressed by the transformation of Kekeya, not only for its greenery, but also for what the trees produced. "It's not just green, but it's practical. It's orchards of apples and other fruits," Weathers said during a visit with international guests. Kekeya's afforestation project, launched in 1986, marks its 40th anniversary this year. The project aimed to combat desertification and reduce the impact of shifting sands and dust storms on nearby residents. Through the sustained efforts of volunteers and forest rangers, about 80,000 hectares of forests were planted from 1986 to 2020. The number of dusty days in nearby Aksu City fell from about 100 in 1980 to around 30 in 2022. For Weathers, who has lived in China for more than two decades, an encounter at the memorial hall brought that history closer. He recalled meeting 81-year-old Imam Memet, the first head of the Kekeya forestry station, which was established in 1986. Meeting a man whose earlier life was documented in the museum's photographs gave the story a human dimension. "His son was with him. And his grandson even helped out as a 12-year-old at the time, just carrying branches and moving things around," Weathers said. Reflecting on the planning behind China's greening efforts, he added that coordination was something he believed the United States could learn from China. Local governments also encouraged residents to help preserve the hard-earned forests while supporting their incomes through the cultivation of cash crops, including apples, walnuts and jujubes. The juicy Aksu apple has become Xinjiang's signature agricultural product. For Ugandan journalist Jenipher Asimwe, the connection between ecological protection and economic activity was a key lesson of the visit. An apple orchard the group visited near the memorial hall left a particularly strong impression on her. She told Xinhua that the orchards demonstrated how restoration could support both environmental protection and local development. The visit reminded her of semi-arid areas in Uganda, where, she said, livestock keepers face water shortages during dry periods. She expressed hope for more cooperation between Uganda and China to explore locally suitable approaches to land restoration and agricultural development. "If you came here, as I did, you cannot even know that it was once a desert," she said. The greening effort has also shaped wider ecological work in Aksu. At a July press conference marking the anniversary, local authorities described how the region had combined ecological restoration with fruit cultivation, processing and other industries. The visit to Kekeya was part of the third installment of the 2026 "Xinjiang in Four Seasons" tour, which brought international social media influencers to cultural sites, agricultural facilities and other destinations across Aksu Prefecture. For Asimwe, the transformation also underscored the importance of sustained effort. "You cannot say that it was a one-day thing," she said. "It was done step by step." ■

item.title: China's storage deployment helping change economics of renewable electricity: IRENA official
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
FUZHOU, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 World Energy Storage Conference runs from Wednesday to Friday in Ningde City, east China's Fujian Province, bringing together participants to discuss cutting-edge technologies, prospects for the energy storage industry, and China's position in the global energy storage market. In 2025, global annual battery storage additions hit roughly 307 GWh, with China accounting for 56 percent. The scale of deployment in China has become central to the global storage market and is "helping to change the economics of renewable electricity," said Ilina Stefanova, head of the Coalition for Action at the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), at the opening ceremony. China's experience in technology, manufacturing, deployment and grid integration will matter not only domestically, but also for the global energy transition, she added. As renewables become a major energy source worldwide, storage is evolving from a supporting facility into essential new infrastructure for power systems. It must meet diverse grid demands while continuously improving reliability and stability, said Zeng Yuqun, founder and chairman of China's leading battery manufacturer CATL, which is based in Ningde City. Industry figures show China is responding to these demands. China's new-type storage industry has achieved notable results, said Xiong Jijun, vice minister of industry and information technology, in the opening speech. China's storage battery output exceeded 420 GWh in the first half of 2026, up about 110 percent year on year. The industry is advancing along multiple technological routes, with lithium batteries playing a leading role alongside sodium-ion and flow batteries. The government will balance development and safety, strengthen technological innovation, adhere to demand-driven principles and foster a global industrial ecosystem, while firmly guarding against rat race competition and guiding the industry from scale expansion toward innovation-led growth, Xiong added. Ningde City has hosted the conference three times previously, an event that has attracted representatives from governments, industries and academia in over 50 countries and regions. ■

item.title: China vows effective measures to deter any sabotaging moves in South China Sea
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- China's defense ministry has vowed to take resolute and effective measures to deter any sabotaging moves in the South China Sea and uphold regional peace and stability. Chen Xi, a spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense, made the statement on Friday in response to a media query concerning the Philippines' recent provocations near China's Huangyan Dao and Ren'ai Jiao, as well as its military's claims about Chinese vessels and China's intentions in the area. China has indisputable sovereignty over Huangyan Dao and Nansha Qundao, including Zhongye Dao, Xianbin Jiao and Ren'ai Jiao, and their adjacent waters, and has sovereign rights and jurisdiction over relevant waters, Chen said. These islands and reefs lie outside Philippine territory. Meanwhile, the Chinese side is taking necessary measures in accordance with relevant laws and regulations to uphold its sovereign rights, which are legitimate, reasonable, professional and standardized, the spokesperson said. For some time, the Philippine side has been rallying external forces to stir up trouble in the South China Sea, while violating others' sovereignty, making provocations and distorting facts to spread false narratives. All these have made the Philippines a destroyer of peace and a destabilizing factor in the South China Sea, Chen said. In response to another media query, the spokesperson slammed Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro's hyping of the South China Sea issue and his false remarks about China. "A certain Philippine politician cares only about his selfish interests, trying to gain political influence by taking an extreme anti-China position, expand his own military power by creating 'external threats,' and trade for foreign support through stirring up trouble in the South China Sea," Chen said. All these moves have directly jeopardized the Philippines' national security and people's well-being, greatly undermined regional peace and stability and the shared interests of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, and had a destructive impact on China-Philippines ties and defense relations, the spokesperson said. The Chinese side remains committed to firmly safeguarding national territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, and building the South China Sea into a sea of peace, friendship and cooperation together with regional countries, he added. ■

item.title: No room for consideration for Japan to follow postwar int'l order, honor obligations: Chinese spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Friday that there is no room for consideration for Japan to follow the postwar international order and honor its international obligations. Spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks in response to a relevant query. According to reports, during a House of Representatives Budget Committee session, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said there was room to consider remarks made by former foreign minister Katsuya Okada suggesting that U.S. nuclear-armed vessels could be allowed to port in Japan during a crisis. Takaichi hinted at the possibility of explicitly stating exceptions to the Three Non-Nuclear Principles. "The remarks once again revealed Japanese authorities' inflating ambitions of possessing nuclear weapons," said Mao, adding that the current Japanese administration has been turning a blind eye to its international obligations on non-proliferation, attempting to progressively ease nuclear restrictions, strengthen the so-called "extended deterrence" arrangement with its allies, ditch the Three Non-Nuclear Principles, and introduce nuclear-powered submarines, and even seeking to deploy nuclear weapons in Japan. "Such moves pose a serious threat to peace and stability in Asia and the wider world," Mao added. Mao noted that Japan should face up to the concerns of the international community, do serious soul-searching on Japanese militarists' past crimes, abandon "remilitarization" and nuclear attempt, and do not stand on the opposite side of the international community once again. When asked to comment on the remarks by Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, who questioned China's criticism against Japan by claiming that countries that do not possess nuclear weapons or strategic bombers are being criticized by countries that possess both, Mao said that as a WWII defeated nation and a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, Japan is obligated under international law to refrain from breaching the exclusively defense-oriented policy and possessing nuclear weapons. "It is high time that Japanese politicians caught up on history and law," Mao added. ■

item.title: U.S. companies to top CIIE exhibition area for eighth straight year
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on preparations for the 9th China International Import Expo, in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Pan Xu) BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- U.S. companies will top the exhibition area at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) for the eighth time, with their area up 1,500 square meters from last year, an official said on Friday. The ninth CIIE will be held in Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10. Launched in 2018 as the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports, the CIIE was designed to expand China's opening up and turn its vast market into a shared opportunity for the world. Preparations for the ninth CIIE are basically complete. A total of 162 countries, regions and international organizations will take part, with 4,142 overseas companies exhibiting, China's Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong told a press conference. The overall exhibition area will exceed 440,000 square meters for the first time. In the enterprise exhibition, companies from the United States, Germany, Britain and France will lead the pack in terms of exhibition space. For the first time, the number of Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders attending the event will surpass 300. Additionally, over 2,000 companies will be exhibiting at the CIIE for the first time. This year's CIIE will feature over 200 representative global debuts and first-time exhibits. A variety of cutting-edge innovations that empower industries and enhance people's lives will be showcased together, including endoscopic surgical robots and cochlear implants. Ahead of this year's CIIE, matchmaking sessions themed under "export to China" were held in countries including Egypt, Germany and Britain, bringing procurement talks to the doorstep of trading partners. The CIIE is a prominent example of China's efforts to expand imports and provide more channels for quality products from around the world to enter the Chinese market. This commitment has remained high on China's agenda, and the results are tangible. According to the General Administration of Customs, China's imports reached 16.7 trillion yuan (about 2.48 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first nine months of this year, up 22.3 percent, the fastest growth since 2021. Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao said earlier this year that China's market holds huge potential, adding that the country will bring in more agricultural goods, quality consumer products, advanced technology equipment and key components. Meanwhile, platforms like the CIIE will be fully used to expand import channels, he said. "Exports and imports are like two wheels of a vehicle. The more balanced they are, the smoother and farther it goes," Wang said. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Hunan University on its centenary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday extended congratulations to faculty, students and alumni of Hunan University as it marks its 100th anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a congratulatory letter to the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward fine revolutionary traditions, continue to elevate the quality and levels of its teaching, and strive to nurture more talent who can apply their knowledge to practical affairs, so as to make new contributions to building China into an education powerhouse and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1926, Hunan University has nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent over the past century. ■

item.title: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, visits the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve in Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Oct. 16, 2026. Xi made an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) ULANQAB, Inner Mongolia, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, talks with staff members while visiting Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Oct. 16, 2026.
